samples.summary: `navigator.clipboard` is undefined on an insecure origin, so the Copy handler throws a TypeError instead of taking the rejection path its own comment describes
samples.evidence: The comment at :89 states "The write can be refused — an insecure origin, a lost focus, a cross-origin frame" and the code handles that with a rejection callback: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(ok, err)`. But on a non-secure context (plain http, the exact case the comment names) `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined` — the expression throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'writeText')` synchronously inside the React onClick, so the rejection handler never runs and the failure is an uncaught exception rather than a warning. A guard (`navigator.clipboard?.writeText(url)?.then(...)` or a try/catch) is needed for the branch the comment claims to cover.

samples.summary: `linkAtMouse` reads `renderedLinks` that can be stale because `renderSheet()` repaints asynchronously, so a click shortly after a scroll can open a URL belonging to a different cell
samples.evidence: `GridCanvas.renderedLinks` is only rebuilt inside `GridCanvas.render()`, which is reached from `Worksheet.renderSheet()` (worksheet.ts:6185) *after* `await sheet.fetchGrid(...)` (:6215) and `await sheet.getStore().listThreads()` (:6222). The scroll handler (:2789) calls `this.resetLinkHover(); ...; this.render();` — but `render()` only schedules the async repaint. Between the scroll event and that repaint, `linkAtMouse` (:931) and `linksInCell` still describe the pre-scroll pixel positions. A mousedown in that window (`handleMouseDown` :3684) therefore resolves the point against boxes that are no longer where the text is, and `window.open(link.url, ...)` navigates to a URL from a cell other than the one under the pointer. The design doc §2 asserts "'the underline is here but the click lands there' is not a reachable state", which holds only for synchronous repaints.

samples.summary: The no-hit fallback in `updateLinkHover` uses `toRefFromMouse`, which disagrees with the painting cell for merged and overflowing cells — the very cells the design doc says the card exists for
samples.evidence: Lines 955-961: when there is no span hit, the code falls back to `toSref(this.toRefFromMouse(x, y))` and only keeps it if `linksInCell(candidate).length > 0`. The comment two blocks above (:946-951) correctly explains that for a merged cell the painter records the anchor's sref while `toRefFromMouse` resolves to a covered sub-cell, and that overflowing text paints outside its own cell. So the fallback — whose stated purpose is "crossing the plain text between two links does not close a card that lists both" (doc §4, `https://a.com and https://b.com`) — returns `[]` for exactly those merged/overflow cells, `sref` becomes null, and the card closes and reopens while the pointer crosses the gap. The failure mode the fallback exists to prevent still occurs in the wide cells that hold several links.

samples.summary: `e.detail === 1` silently suppresses a deliberate second click on a link inside the double-click interval
samples.evidence: `handleMouseDown` gates link opening on `e.detail === 1`. `MouseEvent.detail` is the running click count for consecutive clicks within the platform double-click interval (~500 ms), so a user who plain-clicks (read-only) or Ctrl+clicks a link, then clicks the same link again quickly — e.g. after the new tab failed to open, or to open a second copy — gets `detail === 2` and the branch is skipped entirely: no navigation, and the click falls through to selection with no feedback. Tracking the last-opened URL/time, or moving the open to `click`/`dblclick` suppression, avoids losing the intentional second click.

samples.summary: `toLabel` truncation is off by one and does not bound the label the way its doc comment claims
samples.evidence: `return tail.length > 40 ? `${host}${tail.slice(0, 39)}…` : `${host}${tail}`;` — the threshold is 40 but the slice keeps 39, so a 41-character tail loses two characters rather than one. More substantively, the doc comment says the host "survives truncation and the path gives way", but `host` is prepended at full length in both branches, so the returned label has no upper bound at all; only the CSS `truncate` class actually limits it.

samples.summary: `linkAt` hit test is inclusive on both edges, so two horizontally adjacent link boxes overlap by one pixel
samples.evidence: `x >= link.left && x <= link.left + link.width` (and likewise for y) makes the right/bottom edge belong to the box. For two spans on the same line separated by zero-width text, the right edge of the first and the left edge of the second are the same coordinate, and the first one pushed wins. Half-open bounds (`x < link.left + link.width`) match how `clipLinkBox` computes intersections (`right <= left` ⇒ null).
